reviewerReport.lensLeakageCheck: Every English line of the chapter was read against the Greek. No line adds interpretive content, uses Raëlian-canon vocabulary (no Elohim, Yahweh, craft, creators, ray, planet, Eternals), or resolves an ambiguity in the canon's direction. Each Wheel of Heaven reading sits in its own paragraph headed 'reception note, not a translation claim'. The two lines that coincide with the canon's French were tested specifically: 2:2/2:9 'at its rising' (BDAG ἀνατολή 1 cites both verses; NAB 1970, NRSV, ESV) and 26:53 'put at my disposal' (BDAG παρίστημι 1a cites the verse; NASB identical wording). In both the lexical ground is real and independent of the canon, so neither is lens leakage.
reviewerReport.escalationReportAdjustments: Initial verdicts were formed from the Greek, the chapter JSON, the overlay and the central diff before the escalation report (wave-m2-editor-report.md) was opened. The report added no information that changes a verdict. It repeats the RSV attribution for 2:2/9 ('RSV, NRSV, NAB'), which this review corrects. Its ten founder-preference points are answered in founderDecisionRecommendations, and its follow-ups (17:21; 17:22; comma/colon in 25 and 28; the 6:13 'testing' wording in central) are endorsed as later-pass items.

founderDecisionRecommendations.1-angelos-angel: Endorse. ἄγγελος is the technical term for a heavenly envoy in first-century Jewish Greek (BDAG s.v. 2); published Mt 1, 13, 25, 28, Acts 12 and the Revelation wave all print 'angel', so the Greek NT is already harmonized in practice. Promote jointly with Revelation as a central Greek-NT convention; keep 'messenger of YHWH' for Hebrew malʾāḵ.
founderDecisionRecommendations.2-naos-sanctuary: Endorse for Matthew. The naos/hieron distinction is lexical (BDAG; Josephus) and NRSV marks it in 23:16-35. 27:5 keeps Matthew's crux honestly (and, to my reading, restores the ASV's own 'sanctuary'). If promoted, scope it to books with both terms; Revelation's 'temple' for ναός is defensible because it has no ἱερόν.
founderDecisionRecommendations.3-23:14-no-paragraph: Endorse. SBLGNT has no 23:14; the Byzantine text is quoted in full at 23:13 with witnesses, as the 6:13b precedent and the Revelation ruling C require. Recommend a later pass bring the stable 17:21 into line: its bracketed Greek is not SBLGNT text, so drop the paragraph and move the Byzantine wording into the 17:20 commentary.
founderDecisionRecommendations.4-colon-convention: Endorse (punctuation only; applied without exception in the wave). Harmonize published 25 and 28 in a later pass.
founderDecisionRecommendations.5-magi: Endorse. 'magi' is the standard scholarly rendering (BDAG; Brown; Powell) and NIV/NAB usage; 'wise men' is noted.
founderDecisionRecommendations.6-faithfulness-23:23: Endorse. BDAG lists Mt 23:23 under πίστις 1a 'faithfulness, reliability'; NIV and ESV render so; the Mic 6:8 triad is conduct.
founderDecisionRecommendations.7-put-at-my-disposal-26:53: Endorse. BDAG παρίστημι 1a cites this verse for 'put at someone's disposal', and the NASB prints exactly 'put at My disposal'; the ground is independent of the canon's French, and the coincidence is disclosed.
founderDecisionRecommendations.8-at-its-rising-2:2,9: Endorse. BDAG ἀνατολή 1 cites both verses; NAB (1970, before TBWTT) and NRSV read 'at its rising', ESV 'when it rose'. Correct the RSV attribution (the RSV reads 'in the East').
founderDecisionRecommendations.9-defiles-a-person: Endorse. The article with ἄνθρωπος is generic; the canon's own French « l'homme » is generic too, so the line follows the sense the canon intends rather than the English edition's 'the man'.
founderDecisionRecommendations.10-tempted-4:1: Endorse. Agent-driven 'tempted'/'the tempter' is BDAG's and the versions' reading with the devil as agent, and agrees with published 6:13; the test reading (Gerhardsson; canon « mis à l'épreuve ») is properly in commentary. Optionally align the chapter 4 title ('The testing in the wilderness') with the line.

paragraphs.text: Καὶ προσκαλεσάμενος τοὺς δώδεκα μαθητὰς αὐτοῦ ἔδωκεν αὐτοῖς ἐξουσίαν πνευμάτων ἀκαθάρτων ὥστε ἐκβάλλειν αὐτὰ καὶ θεραπεύειν πᾶσαν νόσον καὶ πᾶσαν μαλακίαν.
paragraphs.translit: kai proskalesamenos tous dōdeka mathētas autou edōken autois exousian pneumatōn akathartōn hōste ekballein auta kai therapeuein pasan noson kai pasan malakian.

i18n.en: And he called to him his twelve disciples and gave them authority over unclean spirits, to cast them out, and to heal every disease and every sickness.

notes.official: *pneumatōn akathartōn* 'unclean spirits': lower case for spirits other than God's (`pneuma-spirit-capitalization-matthew`). The authority given to the twelve repeats the summary of Jesus' own work at 4:23 and 9:35.

paragraphs.text: τῶν δὲ δώδεκα ἀποστόλων τὰ ὀνόματά ἐστιν ταῦτα· πρῶτος Σίμων ὁ λεγόμενος Πέτρος καὶ Ἀνδρέας ὁ ἀδελφὸς αὐτοῦ, Ἰάκωβος ὁ τοῦ Ζεβεδαίου καὶ Ἰωάννης ὁ ἀδελφὸς αὐτοῦ,
paragraphs.translit: tōn de dōdeka apostolōn ta onomata estin tauta· prōtos simōn ho legomenos petros kai andreas ho adelphos autou, iakōbos ho tou zebedaiou kai iōannēs ho adelphos autou,

i18n.en: Now the names of the twelve apostles are these: first, Simon, who is called Peter, and Andrew his brother; James the son of Zebedee, and John his brother;

notes.official: *apostolōn* 'apostles', the only occurrence of the noun in Matthew; it means 'those sent out' (10:5, *apesteilen*).

paragraphs.text: Φίλιππος καὶ Βαρθολομαῖος, Θωμᾶς καὶ Μαθθαῖος ὁ τελώνης, Ἰάκωβος ὁ τοῦ Ἁλφαίου καὶ Θαδδαῖος,
paragraphs.translit: philippos kai bartholomaios, thōmas kai maththaios ho telōnēs, iakōbos ho tou halphaiou kai thaddaios,

i18n.en: Philip and Bartholomew; Thomas and Matthew the tax collector; James the son of Alphaeus, and Thaddaeus;

notes.official: *kai Thaddaios* 'and Thaddaeus' (critical text, with Sinaiticus and Vaticanus). The Byzantine text and the KJV read *Lebbaios ho epiklētheis Thaddaios* 'Lebbaeus, whose surname was Thaddaeus'; Codex Bezae reads *Lebbaios* alone. Luke 6:16 and Acts 1:13 have 'Judas son of James' in this place (Metzger, Textual Commentary, ad loc.; `critical-text-baseline-and-byzantine-variant-recording-matthew`, `proper-names-and-realia-forms-matthew`). 'Matthew the tax collector' identifies the apostle with the man of 9:9.

paragraphs.text: Σίμων ὁ Καναναῖος καὶ Ἰούδας ὁ Ἰσκαριώτης ὁ καὶ παραδοὺς αὐτόν.
paragraphs.translit: simōn ho kananaios kai ioudas ho iskariōtēs ho kai paradous auton.

i18n.en: Simon the Cananaean, and Judas Iscariot, who also handed him over.

notes.official: *Simōn ho Kananaios* 'Simon the Cananaean': the Greek transliterates Aramaic *qanʾānā* 'zealous one', which Luke translates *ho zēlōtēs* 'the Zealot' (Luke 6:15; Acts 1:13). The Byzantine text reads *ho Kananitēs*, which the KJV renders 'the Canaanite', a mistaken association with Canaan (`proper-names-and-realia-forms-matthew`). *ho kai paradous auton* 'who also handed him over': *paradidōmi* is rendered 'hand over' throughout (cf. 4:12; 26:2), where the ASV has 'betrayed'.

paragraphs.text: Τούτους τοὺς δώδεκα ἀπέστειλεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς παραγγείλας αὐτοῖς λέγων· Εἰς ὁδὸν ἐθνῶν μὴ ἀπέλθητε καὶ εἰς πόλιν Σαμαριτῶν μὴ εἰσέλθητε·
paragraphs.translit: toutous tous dōdeka apesteilen ho iēsous parangeilas autois legōn· eis hodon ethnōn mē apelthēte kai eis polin samaritōn mē eiselthēte·

i18n.en: These twelve Jesus sent out, charging them, saying: "Do not go off on the road of the Gentiles, and do not enter a city of the Samaritans;

notes.official: 'Do not go off on the road of the Gentiles, and do not enter a city of the Samaritans': the restriction of the mission to Israel (also 15:24) is lifted only after the resurrection (28:19, 'all the nations').

paragraphs.text: πορεύεσθε δὲ μᾶλλον πρὸς τὰ πρόβατα τὰ ἀπολωλότα οἴκου Ἰσραήλ.
paragraphs.translit: poreuesthe de mallon pros ta probata ta apolōlota oikou israēl.

i18n.en: but go rather to the lost sheep of the house of Israel.

paragraphs.text: πορευόμενοι δὲ κηρύσσετε λέγοντες ὅτι Ἤγγικεν ἡ βασιλεία τῶν οὐρανῶν.
paragraphs.translit: poreuomenoi de kēryssete legontes hoti ēngiken hē basileia tōn ouranōn.

i18n.en: And as you go, proclaim, saying: 'The kingdom of the heavens has come near.'

notes.official: 'proclaim, saying: The kingdom of the heavens has come near': the disciples announce exactly what John (3:2) and Jesus (4:17) announced. The colon follows the convention adopted for this wave (`speech-introduction-colon-convention-matthew`).

paragraphs.text: ἀσθενοῦντας θεραπεύετε, νεκροὺς ἐγείρετε, λεπροὺς καθαρίζετε, δαιμόνια ἐκβάλλετε· δωρεὰν ἐλάβετε, δωρεὰν δότε.
paragraphs.translit: asthenountas therapeuete, nekrous egeirete, leprous katharizete, daimonia ekballete· dōrean elabete, dōrean dote.

i18n.en: Heal the sick, raise the dead, cleanse lepers, cast out demons. You received without payment; give without payment.

notes.official: *nekrous egeirete* 'raise the dead' is in SBLGNT, the TR and the KJV, but absent from most Byzantine manuscripts; its position in the list also varies in the witnesses (Metzger, Textual Commentary, ad loc.; `critical-text-baseline-and-byzantine-variant-recording-matthew`). *leprous katharizete* 'cleanse lepers' (`katharizo-make-clean-leprosy-matthew`). *dōrean* 'without payment', twice.

paragraphs.text: μὴ κτήσησθε χρυσὸν μηδὲ ἄργυρον μηδὲ χαλκὸν εἰς τὰς ζώνας ὑμῶν,
paragraphs.translit: mē ktēsēsthe chryson mēde argyron mēde chalkon eis tas zōnas hymōn,

i18n.en: Do not acquire gold, nor silver, nor copper for your belts,

notes.official:
*Mē ktēsēsthe* 'Do not acquire': *ktaomai* means 'procure, acquire', and only its perfect means 'possess' (BDAG s.v.). The prohibition is against getting money for the mission. *chalkon* 'copper' is the metal of small change, so the series runs gold, silver, copper (`ktaomai-acquire-mt-10-9`). *eis tas zōnas hymōn* 'for your belts': the belt served as a purse.

**Wheel of Heaven reading (reception note, not a translation claim).** The Book Which Tells the Truth (ch. 5) quotes 10:9-10 as « Ne possédez ni or ni argent ni monnaies, dans vos ceintures ; pas de besaces pour le chemin, ni de deuxième tunique, ni de chaussures, ni de bâton » and sets the instruction against the wealth of the Vatican. 'Possess' and 'money' are a paraphrase of the Greek; the line keeps 'acquire' and 'copper'.

paragraphs.text: μὴ πήραν εἰς ὁδὸν μηδὲ δύο χιτῶνας μηδὲ ὑποδήματα μηδὲ ῥάβδον· ἄξιος γὰρ ὁ ἐργάτης τῆς τροφῆς αὐτοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: mē pēran eis hodon mēde dyo chitōnas mēde hypodēmata mēde rhabdon· axios gar ho ergatēs tēs trophēs autou.

i18n.en: no bag for the road, nor two tunics, nor sandals, nor a staff; for the worker is worthy of his food.

notes.official: *pēran* 'bag': a traveller's or beggar's bag (the canon's « besace », EN 'scrip'). Matthew forbids sandals and a staff, which Mark 6:8-9 allows. *axios gar ho ergatēs tēs trophēs autou* 'the worker is worthy of his food'; Luke 10:7 and 1 Tim 5:18 have 'his wages'. See the reception note at 10:9.

paragraphs.text: εἰς ἣν δʼ ἂν πόλιν ἢ κώμην εἰσέλθητε, ἐξετάσατε τίς ἐν αὐτῇ ἄξιός ἐστιν· κἀκεῖ μείνατε ἕως ἂν ἐξέλθητε.
paragraphs.translit: eis hēn dʼ an polin ē kōmēn eiselthēte, exetasate tis en autē axios estin· kakei meinate heōs an exelthēte.

i18n.en: And into whatever city or village you enter, inquire who in it is worthy, and stay there until you depart.

paragraphs.text: εἰσερχόμενοι δὲ εἰς τὴν οἰκίαν ἀσπάσασθε αὐτήν·
paragraphs.translit: eiserchomenoi de eis tēn oikian aspasasthe autēn·

i18n.en: And as you enter the house, greet it.

paragraphs.text: καὶ ἐὰν μὲν ᾖ ἡ οἰκία ἀξία, ἐλθάτω ἡ εἰρήνη ὑμῶν ἐπʼ αὐτήν· ἐὰν δὲ μὴ ᾖ ἀξία, ἡ εἰρήνη ὑμῶν πρὸς ὑμᾶς ἐπιστραφήτω.
paragraphs.translit: kai ean men ē hē oikia axia, elthatō hē eirēnē hymōn epʼ autēn· ean de mē ē axia, hē eirēnē hymōn pros hymas epistraphētō.

i18n.en: And if the house is worthy, let your peace come upon it; but if it is not worthy, let your peace return to you.

paragraphs.text: καὶ ὃς ἂν μὴ δέξηται ὑμᾶς μηδὲ ἀκούσῃ τοὺς λόγους ὑμῶν, ἐξερχόμενοι ἔξω τῆς οἰκίας ἢ τῆς πόλεως ἐκείνης ἐκτινάξατε τὸν κονιορτὸν τῶν ποδῶν ὑμῶν.
paragraphs.translit: kai hos an mē dexētai hymas mēde akousē tous logous hymōn, exerchomenoi exō tēs oikias ē tēs poleōs ekeinēs ektinaxate ton koniorton tōn podōn hymōn.

i18n.en: And whoever does not receive you nor listen to your words, as you go out of that house or that city, shake off the dust of your feet.

paragraphs.text: ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν, ἀνεκτότερον ἔσται γῇ Σοδόμων καὶ Γομόρρων ἐν ἡμέρᾳ κρίσεως ἢ τῇ πόλει ἐκείνῃ.
paragraphs.translit: amēn legō hymin, anektoteron estai gē sodomōn kai gomorrōn en hēmera kriseōs ē tē polei ekeinē.

i18n.en: Amen I say to you, it will be more tolerable for the land of Sodom and Gomorrah on the day of judgment than for that city.

notes.official: 'the land of Sodom and Gomorrah' (Gen 19): the cities stand for exemplary judgment, as in 11:23-24.

paragraphs.text: Ἰδοὺ ἐγὼ ἀποστέλλω ὑμᾶς ὡς πρόβατα ἐν μέσῳ λύκων· γίνεσθε οὖν φρόνιμοι ὡς οἱ ὄφεις καὶ ἀκέραιοι ὡς αἱ περιστεραί.
paragraphs.translit: idou egō apostellō hymas hōs probata en mesō lykōn· ginesthe oun phronimoi hōs hoi opheis kai akeraioi hōs hai peristerai.

i18n.en: Behold, I am sending you out as sheep in the midst of wolves; so be wise as serpents and innocent as doves.

notes.official: *akeraioi* 'innocent', literally 'unmixed', i.e. without guile.

paragraphs.text: προσέχετε δὲ ἀπὸ τῶν ἀνθρώπων· παραδώσουσιν γὰρ ὑμᾶς εἰς συνέδρια, καὶ ἐν ταῖς συναγωγαῖς αὐτῶν μαστιγώσουσιν ὑμᾶς·
paragraphs.translit: prosechete de apo tōn anthrōpōn· paradōsousin gar hymas eis synedria, kai en tais synagōgais autōn mastigōsousin hymas·

i18n.en: But beware of people; for they will hand you over to councils, and in their synagogues they will flog you;

notes.official: *prosechete de apo tōn anthrōpōn* 'But beware of people': generic plural (`anthropos-generic-people-convention-matthew`). *synedria* 'councils': local Jewish courts, distinct from the Sanhedrin of 26:59.

paragraphs.text: καὶ ἐπὶ ἡγεμόνας δὲ καὶ βασιλεῖς ἀχθήσεσθε ἕνεκεν ἐμοῦ εἰς μαρτύριον αὐτοῖς καὶ τοῖς ἔθνεσιν.
paragraphs.translit: kai epi hēgemonas de kai basileis achthēsesthe heneken emou eis martyrion autois kai tois ethnesin.

i18n.en: and you will be brought before governors and kings for my sake, as a testimony to them and to the Gentiles.

paragraphs.text: ὅταν δὲ παραδῶσιν ὑμᾶς, μὴ μεριμνήσητε πῶς ἢ τί λαλήσητε· δοθήσεται γὰρ ὑμῖν ἐν ἐκείνῃ τῇ ὥρᾳ τί λαλήσητε·
paragraphs.translit: hotan de paradōsin hymas, mē merimnēsēte pōs ē ti lalēsēte· dothēsetai gar hymin en ekeinē tē hōra ti lalēsēte·

i18n.en: But when they hand you over, do not be anxious how or what you are to speak; for what you are to speak will be given to you in that hour.

paragraphs.text: οὐ γὰρ ὑμεῖς ἐστε οἱ λαλοῦντες ἀλλὰ τὸ πνεῦμα τοῦ πατρὸς ὑμῶν τὸ λαλοῦν ἐν ὑμῖν.
paragraphs.translit: ou gar hymeis este hoi lalountes alla to pneuma tou patros hymōn to laloun en hymin.

i18n.en: For it is not you who speak, but the Spirit of your Father who speaks in you.

notes.official: *to pneuma tou patros hymōn* 'the Spirit of your Father', the divine Spirit, capitalized (`pneuma-spirit-capitalization-matthew`).

paragraphs.text: παραδώσει δὲ ἀδελφὸς ἀδελφὸν εἰς θάνατον καὶ πατὴρ τέκνον, καὶ ἐπαναστήσονται τέκνα ἐπὶ γονεῖς καὶ θανατώσουσιν αὐτούς.
paragraphs.translit: paradōsei de adelphos adelphon eis thanaton kai patēr teknon, kai epanastēsontai tekna epi goneis kai thanatōsousin autous.

i18n.en: And brother will hand over brother to death, and a father his child; and children will rise up against parents and have them put to death.

paragraphs.text: καὶ ἔσεσθε μισούμενοι ὑπὸ πάντων διὰ τὸ ὄνομά μου· ὁ δὲ ὑπομείνας εἰς τέλος οὗτος σωθήσεται.
paragraphs.translit: kai esesthe misoumenoi hypo pantōn dia to onoma mou· ho de hypomeinas eis telos houtos sōthēsetai.

i18n.en: And you will be hated by all for my name's sake; but the one who endures to the end, this one will be saved.

paragraphs.text: ὅταν δὲ διώκωσιν ὑμᾶς ἐν τῇ πόλει ταύτῃ, φεύγετε εἰς τὴν ἑτέραν· ἀμὴν γὰρ λέγω ὑμῖν, οὐ μὴ τελέσητε τὰς πόλεις τοῦ Ἰσραὴλ ἕως ἂν ἔλθῃ ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου.
paragraphs.translit: hotan de diōkōsin hymas en tē polei tautē, pheugete eis tēn heteran· amēn gar legō hymin, ou mē telesēte tas poleis tou israēl heōs an elthē ho huios tou anthrōpou.

i18n.en: But when they persecute you in this city, flee to the next; for amen I say to you, you will not finish going through the cities of Israel before the Son of Man comes.

notes.official: 'you will not finish going through the cities of Israel before the Son of Man comes': one of the most discussed sayings of the Gospel; A. Schweitzer made it the hinge of his reading of Jesus' expectation of an imminent end (The Quest of the Historical Jesus, 1906). It is translated as written (`son-of-man-bar-enash-dan-7-13-mt-cross-corpus`).

paragraphs.text: Οὐκ ἔστιν μαθητὴς ὑπὲρ τὸν διδάσκαλον οὐδὲ δοῦλος ὑπὲρ τὸν κύριον αὐτοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: ouk estin mathētēs hyper ton didaskalon oude doulos hyper ton kyrion autou.

i18n.en: A disciple is not above his teacher, nor a slave above his master.

notes.official: *didaskalos* 'teacher', *kyrios* 'master' (in the image of a slave and his owner); the compound *oikodespotēs* in 10:25 is also 'master (of the house)'. In 23:8-10 'teacher' renders *didaskalos*, and *kathēgētēs* is rendered 'instructor' to keep the titles of that passage distinct.

paragraphs.text: ἀρκετὸν τῷ μαθητῇ ἵνα γένηται ὡς ὁ διδάσκαλος αὐτοῦ, καὶ ὁ δοῦλος ὡς ὁ κύριος αὐτοῦ. εἰ τὸν οἰκοδεσπότην Βεελζεβοὺλ ἐπεκάλεσαν, πόσῳ μᾶλλον τοὺς οἰκιακοὺς αὐτοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: arketon tō mathētē hina genētai hōs ho didaskalos autou, kai ho doulos hōs ho kyrios autou. ei ton oikodespotēn beelzeboul epekalesan, posō mallon tous oikiakous autou.

i18n.en: It is enough for the disciple that he become like his teacher, and the slave like his master. If they have called the master of the house Beelzebul, how much more will they call those of his household.

notes.official: *Beelzeboul* 'Beelzebul' (SBLGNT). Vaticanus and Sinaiticus read *Beezeboul*; the Vulgate, the Syriac and the KJV read 'Beelzebub', assimilating to *baʿal zəḇûḇ* 'lord of flies', the god of Ekron in 2 Kgs 1:2. *Beelzeboul* is usually explained from *baʿal zəḇûl* 'lord of the (exalted) dwelling', with a play on *oikodespotēs* 'master of the house' in this verse (`proper-names-and-realia-forms-matthew`; `critical-text-baseline-and-byzantine-variant-recording-matthew`). The accusation of collusion with a demonic power is the same charge as 9:34 and 12:24.

paragraphs.text: Μὴ οὖν φοβηθῆτε αὐτούς· οὐδὲν γάρ ἐστιν κεκαλυμμένον ὃ οὐκ ἀποκαλυφθήσεται, καὶ κρυπτὸν ὃ οὐ γνωσθήσεται.
paragraphs.translit: mē oun phobēthēte autous· ouden gar estin kekalymmenon ho ouk apokalyphthēsetai, kai krypton ho ou gnōsthēsetai.

i18n.en: So do not fear them; for there is nothing covered that will not be revealed, and hidden that will not be made known.

paragraphs.text: ὃ λέγω ὑμῖν ἐν τῇ σκοτίᾳ, εἴπατε ἐν τῷ φωτί· καὶ ὃ εἰς τὸ οὖς ἀκούετε, κηρύξατε ἐπὶ τῶν δωμάτων.
paragraphs.translit: ho legō hymin en tē skotia, eipate en tō phōti· kai ho eis to ous akouete, kēryxate epi tōn dōmatōn.

i18n.en: What I tell you in the darkness, speak in the light; and what you hear whispered in your ear, proclaim upon the housetops.

paragraphs.text: καὶ μὴ φοβεῖσθε ἀπὸ τῶν ἀποκτεννόντων τὸ σῶμα τὴν δὲ ψυχὴν μὴ δυναμένων ἀποκτεῖναι· φοβεῖσθε δὲ μᾶλλον τὸν δυνάμενον καὶ ψυχὴν καὶ σῶμα ἀπολέσαι ἐν γεέννῃ.
paragraphs.translit: kai mē phobeisthe apo tōn apoktennontōn to sōma tēn de psychēn mē dynamenōn apokteinai· phobeisthe de mallon ton dynamenon kai psychēn kai sōma apolesai en geennē.

i18n.en: And do not fear those who kill the body but are not able to kill the soul; but rather fear him who is able to destroy both soul and body in gehenna.

notes.official: *psychē* is rendered 'soul' here and 'life' at 10:39. In 10:28 it is set against *sōma* 'body' as what cannot be killed, and only 'soul' says that in English; at 10:39 the saying concerns one's life. The ASV and every major version make the same distinction (`psyche-soul-life-matthew`). *en geennē* 'in gehenna', lower case as in the published 5:22, 29-30: the valley of Hinnom south of Jerusalem (Jer 7:31-32), a name for the place of final punishment.

paragraphs.text: οὐχὶ δύο στρουθία ἀσσαρίου πωλεῖται; καὶ ἓν ἐξ αὐτῶν οὐ πεσεῖται ἐπὶ τὴν γῆν ἄνευ τοῦ πατρὸς ὑμῶν.
paragraphs.translit: ouchi dyo strouthia assariou pōleitai; kai hen ex autōn ou peseitai epi tēn gēn aneu tou patros hymōn.

i18n.en: Are not two sparrows sold for an assarion? And not one of them will fall to the ground apart from your Father.

notes.official: *assariou* 'an assarion': a small Roman bronze coin, one sixteenth of a denarius. The coin name is transliterated, as the published 5:26 keeps 'quadrans' (`proper-names-and-realia-forms-matthew`). *aneu tou patros hymōn* 'apart from your Father'.

paragraphs.text: ὑμῶν δὲ καὶ αἱ τρίχες τῆς κεφαλῆς πᾶσαι ἠριθμημέναι εἰσίν.
paragraphs.translit: hymōn de kai hai triches tēs kephalēs pasai ērithmēmenai eisin.

i18n.en: But even the hairs of your head are all numbered.

paragraphs.text: μὴ οὖν φοβεῖσθε· πολλῶν στρουθίων διαφέρετε ὑμεῖς.
paragraphs.translit: mē oun phobeisthe· pollōn strouthiōn diapherete hymeis.

i18n.en: So do not fear; you are of more value than many sparrows.

paragraphs.text: Πᾶς οὖν ὅστις ὁμολογήσει ἐν ἐμοὶ ἔμπροσθεν τῶν ἀνθρώπων, ὁμολογήσω κἀγὼ ἐν αὐτῷ ἔμπροσθεν τοῦ πατρός μου τοῦ ἐν οὐρανοῖς·
paragraphs.translit: pas oun hostis homologēsei en emoi emprosthen tōn anthrōpōn, homologēsō kagō en autō emprosthen tou patros mou tou en ouranois·

i18n.en: Everyone therefore who will confess me before people, I also will confess him before my Father who is in the heavens;

notes.official:
*hostis homologēsei en emoi … homologēsō kagō en autō* 'Everyone who will confess me … I also will confess him': literally 'confess in me … in him', a Semitic construction (Aramaic *ʾôḏê bə-*). *emprosthen tōn anthrōpōn* 'before people' (`anthropos-generic-people-convention-matthew`). *en tois ouranois* 'in the heavens', plural as in Matthew's other uses of the phrase.

**Wheel of Heaven reading (reception note, not a translation claim).** The Book Which Tells the Truth (ch. 4) quotes 10:32 (« … devant mon père qui est dans les cieux », EN 'before my father which is in heaven') and comments: 'He is "in heaven". Everything is said here', reading the Father as a being located in space, not an immaterial God. The line keeps the Greek plural 'in the heavens' and the generic 'people', where the canon's English has 'men'.

paragraphs.text: ὅστις δʼ ἂν ἀρνήσηταί με ἔμπροσθεν τῶν ἀνθρώπων, ἀρνήσομαι κἀγὼ αὐτὸν ἔμπροσθεν τοῦ πατρός μου τοῦ ἐν οὐρανοῖς.
paragraphs.translit: hostis dʼ an arnēsētai me emprosthen tōn anthrōpōn, arnēsomai kagō auton emprosthen tou patros mou tou en ouranois.

i18n.en: but whoever will deny me before people, I also will deny him before my Father who is in the heavens.

notes.official: 'deny ... before people': the negative counterpart of 10:32, fulfilled in Peter's denials (26:70-74).

paragraphs.text: Μὴ νομίσητε ὅτι ἦλθον βαλεῖν εἰρήνην ἐπὶ τὴν γῆν· οὐκ ἦλθον βαλεῖν εἰρήνην ἀλλὰ μάχαιραν.
paragraphs.translit: mē nomisēte hoti ēlthon balein eirēnēn epi tēn gēn· ouk ēlthon balein eirēnēn alla machairan.

i18n.en: Do not think that I came to bring peace upon the earth; I did not come to bring peace, but a sword.

paragraphs.text: ἦλθον γὰρ διχάσαι ἄνθρωπον κατὰ τοῦ πατρὸς αὐτοῦ καὶ θυγατέρα κατὰ τῆς μητρὸς αὐτῆς καὶ νύμφην κατὰ τῆς πενθερᾶς αὐτῆς,
paragraphs.translit: ēlthon gar dichasai anthrōpon kata tou patros autou kai thygatera kata tēs mētros autēs kai nymphēn kata tēs pentheras autēs,

i18n.en: For I came to set a man against his father, and a daughter against her mother, and a daughter-in-law against her mother-in-law;

notes.official: 10:35-36 adapt Mic 7:6 ('a man's enemies are the men of his own house').

paragraphs.text: καὶ ἐχθροὶ τοῦ ἀνθρώπου οἱ οἰκιακοὶ αὐτοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: kai echthroi tou anthrōpou hoi oikiakoi autou.

i18n.en: and a man's enemies will be those of his own household.

paragraphs.text: ὁ φιλῶν πατέρα ἢ μητέρα ὑπὲρ ἐμὲ οὐκ ἔστιν μου ἄξιος· καὶ ὁ φιλῶν υἱὸν ἢ θυγατέρα ὑπὲρ ἐμὲ οὐκ ἔστιν μου ἄξιος·
paragraphs.translit: ho philōn patera ē mētera hyper eme ouk estin mou axios· kai ho philōn huion ē thygatera hyper eme ouk estin mou axios·

i18n.en: The one who loves father or mother more than me is not worthy of me; and the one who loves son or daughter more than me is not worthy of me;

paragraphs.text: καὶ ὃς οὐ λαμβάνει τὸν σταυρὸν αὐτοῦ καὶ ἀκολουθεῖ ὀπίσω μου, οὐκ ἔστιν μου ἄξιος.
paragraphs.translit: kai hos ou lambanei ton stauron autou kai akolouthei opisō mou, ouk estin mou axios.

i18n.en: and whoever does not take his cross and follow after me is not worthy of me.

notes.official: *ton stauron autou* 'his cross': the first mention of the cross in Matthew, before any passion prediction.

paragraphs.text: ὁ εὑρὼν τὴν ψυχὴν αὐτοῦ ἀπολέσει αὐτήν, καὶ ὁ ἀπολέσας τὴν ψυχὴν αὐτοῦ ἕνεκεν ἐμοῦ εὑρήσει αὐτήν.
paragraphs.translit: ho heurōn tēn psychēn autou apolesei autēn, kai ho apolesas tēn psychēn autou heneken emou heurēsei autēn.

i18n.en: The one who has found his life will lose it, and the one who has lost his life for my sake will find it.

notes.official: *ho heurōn tēn psychēn autou apolesei autēn* 'The one who has found his life will lose it': *psychē* is 'life' here, unlike 10:28 (`psyche-soul-life-matthew`).

paragraphs.text: Ὁ δεχόμενος ὑμᾶς ἐμὲ δέχεται, καὶ ὁ ἐμὲ δεχόμενος δέχεται τὸν ἀποστείλαντά με.
paragraphs.translit: ho dechomenos hymas eme dechetai, kai ho eme dechomenos dechetai ton aposteilanta me.

i18n.en: The one who receives you receives me, and the one who receives me receives him who sent me.

paragraphs.text: ὁ δεχόμενος προφήτην εἰς ὄνομα προφήτου μισθὸν προφήτου λήμψεται, καὶ ὁ δεχόμενος δίκαιον εἰς ὄνομα δικαίου μισθὸν δικαίου λήμψεται.
paragraphs.translit: ho dechomenos prophētēn eis onoma prophētou misthon prophētou lēmpsetai, kai ho dechomenos dikaion eis onoma dikaiou misthon dikaiou lēmpsetai.

i18n.en: The one who receives a prophet in the name of a prophet will receive a prophet's reward, and the one who receives a righteous man in the name of a righteous man will receive a righteous man's reward.

notes.official: *eis onoma prophētou* 'in the name of a prophet': a Semitic idiom (*ləšēm*) meaning 'because he is a prophet'.

paragraphs.text: καὶ ὃς ἂν ποτίσῃ ἕνα τῶν μικρῶν τούτων ποτήριον ψυχροῦ μόνον εἰς ὄνομα μαθητοῦ, ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν, οὐ μὴ ἀπολέσῃ τὸν μισθὸν αὐτοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: kai hos an potisē hena tōn mikrōn toutōn potērion psychrou monon eis onoma mathētou, amēn legō hymin, ou mē apolesē ton misthon autou.

i18n.en: And whoever gives one of these little ones only a cup of cold water to drink in the name of a disciple, amen I say to you, he will by no means lose his reward."

editorial_questions_resolved.issue: Textual variant: the critical text reads καὶ Θαδδαῖος ('and Thaddaeus'); the Byzantine/TR text (KJV) reads Λεββαῖος ὁ ἐπικληθεὶς Θαδδαῖος ('Lebbaeus, whose surname was Thaddaeus'); Codex Bezae (D) reads Λεββαῖος alone.
Textual variant and rendering: the critical text reads ὁ Καναναῖος (from Aramaic qanʾana 'zealot'); the Byzantine/TR text reads ὁ Κανανίτης, which the KJV renders 'the Canaanite'.
editorial_questions_resolved.resolution: 'the Cananaean' kept (transliteration of Aramaic qanʾana); 'Zealot' meaning and KJV 'Canaanite' error in commentary.

editorial_questions_resolved.issue: Textual variant: νεκροὺς ἐγείρετε ('raise the dead') is present in SBLGNT and the TR/KJV, but absent from the bulk of the Byzantine (Majority) tradition; its position within the list also varies across witnesses.
editorial_questions_resolved.resolution: 'raise the dead' kept (SBLGNT, TR); Majority-text omission recorded.

editorial_questions_resolved.issue: Canon-wording difference: TBWTT ch. 5 quotes 10:9-10 as « Ne possédez ni or ni argent ni monnaies, dans vos ceintures ; pas de besaces pour le chemin… » — μὴ κτήσησθε 'do not acquire / provide' rendered 'possess', and χαλκόν (copper, i.e. small coin) rendered 'money'; πήραν rendered « besace » (scrip/bag).
editorial_questions_resolved.default_taken: Do not acquire gold, nor silver, nor copper
editorial_questions_resolved.resolution: 'Do not acquire ... copper' kept (κτάομαι = acquire, BDAG); canon's 'possess ... money' in reception note.

editorial_questions_resolved.issue: Textual variant: the critical text reads Βεελζεβούλ (Beelzebul); Vaticanus and Sinaiticus read Βεεζεβούλ (Beezebul); the Vulgate, Syriac and KJV read 'Beelzebub' (assimilating to 2 Kgs 1:2 בַּעַל זְבוּב). Draft follows SBLGNT.

ψυχή (psychē) is rendered 'soul' at 10:28 (body/soul contrast) but 'life' at 10:39 (ASV 'life' in both 10:39 clauses; cf. 2:20 'the child's life'). The lexeme switch on the English surface is unglossed.
editorial_questions_resolved.resolution: 'soul' (10:28, body/soul contrast; 26:38) / 'life' (2:20; 10:39; published 6:25), as in all major versions.

editorial_questions_resolved.issue: ὁμολογήσει ἐν ἐμοί … ὁμολογήσω κἀγὼ ἐν αὐτῷ (Semitic 'confess in me'): rendered as the canonical 'confess me … confess him' (ASV; TBWTT ch. 4 « m'avouera … je l'avouerai »). The canon's « mon père qui est dans les cieux » matches the plural τοῖς οὐρανοῖς rendered 'the heavens' per program convention.
editorial_questions_resolved.resolution: 'confess me ... confess him' kept; 'before people' per convention; canon's 'men' and 'in heaven' recorded in reception note.
